cue: Colour is mostly lost to this animal, and its sharpness is about a tenth of yours.

cpd.note: a middle value across the records of inside taxa

fov.note: the panoramic field of dolphins, with the eyes set to the side

gain.note: the app's choice; the records give only a relative sensitivity

whale_mono.note: one cone class, so the picture is drawn in one channel

rows: Whales and seals have only one kind of cone, so they are essentially colour-blind. We show the picture in one channel, as a grey-level world.

A bottlenose dolphin resolves about 2.4 to 4.8 cycles per degree, and a harbour seal about 8.7 to 11.5. Most of the others sit near 3. We blur the picture to about 3.3, which is a tenth or less of your 30.
A dolphin sees a panoramic field of 120 to 130 degrees, with the two eyes overlapping by only 20 to 30 degrees. We draw that field as wide, with a narrow overlap in front.
Dim light and the app's choices
The gain of 1.5 is the app's choice. Dolphins are about half a log unit more sensitive than people in low light, but no record gives a gain figure, so we lift the shadows a little.
Some settings in this view are the app's own choices, because no measurement gives them. They are set to give a fair picture of the animal and can be tuned by hand.

field.name: wedge
field.note: default: the panoramic field of the animal
